clue.text: Put off remit, having to squeeze pus out

indicators.note: squeezing something in means holding it inside, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: to remit something is to send it, as with a payment

indicators.note: out here means disordered, so the three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop work while a spot is lanced and the pus pressed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off' looks like part of the surface's medical scene, but it is the definition; 'out' jumbles to USP, which 'having to squeeze' holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend an event is to postpone it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Three characters needed to produce modest drink

definitions.text: Three characters needed to produce modest drink

parts.words: Three characters needed to produce modest drink
parts.note: three letters of the alphabet, said as a spoken list with 'and' before the last, run together into the name of a weak beer mix

explanation.walkthrough: List the letters S, H and Y aloud as 'S, H and Y' and the words run together give the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy mixes beer with lemonade, so it is a weak, unassuming drink.

clue.text: Fruit drink

definitions.meaning: a gourd such as a butternut is botanically a fruit
a sweet concentrate diluted with water, as in orange cordial

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a gourd vegetable-fruit and a diluted fruit cordial.

clue.text: Beautiful thing, old solver caught in embrace of wayward teacher

indicators.note: being held in someone's embrace means sitting inside them, so these letters go within the rearranged word
wayward means straying, so the letters of teacher are jumbled

parts.note: the solver is 'you', and an archaic form of you is ye
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An elderly crossword fan gets hugged by a wild schoolmistress, who catches the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solver' hints at the reader, addressed in old English as ye; 'wayward' scrambles to E-ATCHER, and 'in embrace of' holds the inner pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking that draws the gaze is an attractive, beautiful object.

clue.text: Drink tops a performance

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sitting on top of another comes first

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Alcohol crowns a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play, a theatrical performance.

clue.text: A little money causes discomfort for those on reservation

parts.note: p stands for penny, a small coin
aches are pains or discomfort

explanation.surface: A small sum of cash brings trouble to someone who has booked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reservation' sounds like a booking, but it is a Native American reservation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a Native American people, many of whom live on reservations.

clue.text: Viewer's favourite to lift drink

parts.note: the viewer is the eye, and a favourite is the apple of one's eye
to jack something up is to raise it

explanation.surface: A TV audience's preferred star raises a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Applejack is an American apple brandy, a strong drink.

clue.text: Drink's shown up in fruit salad

indicators.note: shown up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Alcohol appears in a fruit salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters held within 'fruit salad', and 'shown up' reads them upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine; the clue's 'Drink's' means 'drink is' before 'shown up'.

clue.text: West Sussex town shouldn't get cold feet?

definitions.meaning: a town near Burgess Hill in southern England
someone who ... on ought to keep warm toes

explanation.surface: A Sussex town ought to be immune from nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassocks is a West Sussex town; split as 'has socks' it describes someone with warm feet.

clue.text: Agents turn up round Piccadilly establishment, demanding drink

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece encloses the other
in a down entry turning up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: sales reps act as agents for a firm
the Ritz is a famous hotel on Piccadilly in London

explanation.surface: Salesmen arrive at a London hotel and order a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: Piccadilly is a grand London street, home of the Ritz hotel; 'turn up' gives SPER, read upwards in this down light, and 'round' wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritzer is wine mixed with soda water, a drink.

clue.text: President admits his country getting maltreatment

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Abe is short for Abraham Lincoln, US President
the USA was Lincoln's country

explanation.surface: A head of state confesses his nation is being mistreated.
explanation.definitionFit: Abuse is cruel treatment, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Stimulating drink, perhaps — favourite one absorbed by fermented pears

indicators.note: absorbed by means soaked up inside, so these letters go within the other piece
fermenting changes a thing's makeup, so the letters of pears are rearranged

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Perry, a pear cider, makes a tempting pre-dinner drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks a starter of this kind as one example; 'fermented' scrambles to AP-SER, and 'absorbed by' holds the inner piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif sharpens the appetite, so it is a stimulating drink, among other starters.

clue.text: Eighth Earl Spencer was furious, being criticised

parts.note: the 8th Earl Spencer was Princess Diana's father, so Di's pa
raged means was furious

explanation.surface: Diana's father lost his temper at being attacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Diana, known as Di, was the daughter of the 8th Earl Spencer.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage is to belittle, so disparaged means criticised.

clue.text: Drink from one side of vessel

definitions.meaning: the left side of a ship facing forward

explanation.definitionFit: Port is a fortified wine and also the left-hand side of a ship.

clue.text: Approach menacingly with something hairy, wearing nobody else's

parts.note: a beard is a growth of facial hair
one's own belongs to nobody else
having clothes on means wearing them

explanation.surface: A man with a beard wears borrowed clothes that are his alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear down on someone is to advance threateningly towards them, an idiom.

clue.text: Liquid food makes dog suffer bladder weakness, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the sound of the words gives the answer

parts.note: a cocker spaniel is a dog, and one with bladder weakness is leaky

explanation.surface: Some soup causes the dog to wet itself.
explanation.walkthrough: COCKER LEAKY, said aloud, sounds like the Scottish soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock-a-leekie is a Scottish soup of chicken and leeks, a liquid food.

clue.text: Turning round politician is a job for me

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: coiling means winding or turning round
MP is a member of parliament

explanation.surface: Spinning on the spot, a politician's lot is an occupation for me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the setter, whose job is setting the crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting a crossword is the work of its setter, the 'me' of the clue.

clue.text: Stopping kind of mechanism in the drink

parts.note: ABS is an anti-lock braking system on cars
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A braking system lands in the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the drink' sounds like being in water, but the last word alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong anise-flavoured spirit, a drink.

clue.text: Drink Frenchman's sauce up

indicators.note: in a down entry up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: Rene is a French man's name, so Rene's
sauce and lip both mean cheek

explanation.surface: Drink a French chap's gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RENES LIP as a whole into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilsener is a pale lager, a drink.

clue.text: Drink brings tough old bird to God

parts.note: a boiler is an old hen too tough to roast, fit only for boiling
God is the Maker, the creator

explanation.surface: A drink takes an old hen up to heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: A boilermaker is a shot of whiskey with a beer chaser, a drink.

clue.text: Extent of error to ruin drink

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Tolerance in error is spoilt by a gin.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin of error is the allowed extent by which a figure may be wrong.

clue.text: Roman general rejects posh drink

indicators.note: rejects means throws out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Cassius was a Roman general who plotted against Caesar
U means upper class, posh

explanation.surface: A Roman commander turns down a smart drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassis is a blackcurrant liqueur, a drink.

clue.text: Trendy, the way of the month

parts.note: in means fashionable
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Fashionable, the route of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inst.' was formerly used in business letters for 'of this month'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inst, short for instant, means of the current month in old letter style.

clue.text: Little drink knocked back, then a drink, then beginning to drink a drink

indicators.note: knocked back means turned backwards, as well as gulped

parts.note: a nip is a small measure of spirits
cola is a fizzy soft drink

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A drinker swallows a small one, then another, then starts again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reverses NIP to PIN; the final 'drink' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pina colada is a cocktail of rum, coconut and pineapple.

clue.text: Don't prepare a day before party

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party

explanation.surface: Skip planning the day before a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To ad lib is to improvise, speaking without preparation.

clue.text: Mouth one very dry place

parts.note: gob is slang for mouth
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One mouth is in a parched place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a desert in Mongolia and China, a very dry place.

clue.text: No tailors confused by those with scissors

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: No tailors are puzzled by people with scissors.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonsorial means relating to barbers, who work with scissors.

clue.text: Drink ends in addiction — come along you alcoholics!

indicators.note: ends in picks the last letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: A call to drinkers to join in comes at the end of an addiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus is hot wine mixed with water, sugar and spices.

clue.text: One may dangle each bishop in gravy at first

parts.note: RR is the Right Reverend, a bishop's title
taken as written

indicators.note: at first takes the first letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Every prelate ends up in the gravy at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An earring hangs from an ear, so it is something that may dangle.

clue.text: Fruit from islands replacing meat with bread

indicators.note: replacing says one part of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: the Bahamas are a chain of islands
ham is meat
nan is Indian flatbread

explanation.surface: A fruit from Caribbean islands swaps meat for bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps HAM in BAHAMAS for NAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas are a tropical fruit.
